column1: # Hindi word-level respellings. Each row fixes one measured espeak-ng `hi` error (docs/pronunciation.md, probe in
# bench/results/pronunciation_probe_v7.tsv). Keys are NFC. A row applies only when its category is enabled
# schwa respellings put an explicit virama where espeak keeps a schwa a native speaker drops (or a schwa where espeak
# drops one); they are text tricks for espeak-based engines, not correct orthography.

column4: espeak reads the letters (jəh, "yah"); colloquial Hindi is yeh [jeː]
espeak reads the letters (ʋəh, "vah"); colloquial Hindi is vo [ʋoː]
espeak jˈʌnəʋɾi (janavri) keeps the schwa after न and drops the one after व; Hindi is jan-va-ri
espeak dˈʌʃəmˌələʋ (4 syllables); Hindi is dash-ma-lav
espeak halcˈal (full a vowels, not schwas); Hindi is həl-chəl
espeak nˌəmskˈaːɾ (namskaar) drops the schwa before स्क; Hindi is na-mas-kaar
espeak ɾˈaːməcɾɪt (raamacharit) keeps the schwa after म and drops the one after च; the compound is raam-cha-rit
espeak hˈʌnsənˌaː (hansanaa) keeps the schwa after स; Hindi is hans-naa
the letter name F: espeak reads फ as aspirated pʰ (ˈeːpʰ, "ep"); it is [ɛf] (used in PDF, HDFC, IFSC, FD, FAQ)
espeak kˈʌɾəʋˌəʈ (karavat) keeps the schwa after र; Hindi is kar-vat
espeak zˈĩdɡˌi (zindgi) drops the schwa after द; Hindi is zin-da-gi
espeak ˌĩtzˈaːɾ (intzaar) drops the schwa after त; spoken in-ta/ti/te-zaar, the i spelling keeps a vowel there
